title: Pseudo entropy from entanglement entropy
authors: Abhigyan Saha, Piotr Sułkowski, Tadashi Takayanagi
abstract: Pseudo entropy extends entanglement entropy from a single quantum state to a pair of nonorthogonal states and is generally complex. Taking advantage of Cauchy-Riemann equations, Kramers-Kronig relations, and analytic continuation in state parameters, we show how and to what extent real and imaginary parts of pseudo entropy can be derived from ordinary entanglement entropy. For families with holomorphic coefficients in finite-dimensional Hilbert spaces, the reduced transition matrix equals the ordinary reduced density matrix formula evaluated at complex parameters. Then a convergent Taylor series gives the real and imaginary parts of pseudo entropy from even and odd derivatives of entanglement entropy at the real midpoint. The matrix identity also gives formulae for excess pseudo entropy and Renyi entropies, and interpolation formulae for families with polynomial coefficients. We apply these results to boundary-state quenches and thermal states in conformal field theory, and to fermionic and bosonic Gaussian states and quenches. In conformal field theory, Kramers-Kronig relations give the first moment of the imaginary part in terms of the central charge and one-point functions for boundary states.
summary: This theoretical paper introduces 'pseudo entropy' as an extension of entanglement entropy to pairs of nonorthogonal quantum states. It develops a powerful mathematical toolkit using complex analysis (like Kramers-Kronig relations) to derive the real and imaginary components of this pseudo entropy from standard entanglement entropy. The results are applied to model complex quantum phenomena in CFT and Gaussian states.
main_problem: The paper addresses the mathematical challenge of extending entanglement entropy, which is defined for a single state, to a complex quantity called 'pseudo entropy' for a pair of nonorthogonal states.
main_result: It derives explicit formulas for the real and imaginary parts of pseudo entropy using analytic continuation techniques, relating them to derivatives of the standard entanglement entropy.
method: The core methodology involves leveraging Cauchy-Riemann equations, Kramers-Kronig relations, and Taylor series expansions applied to the reduced transition matrix derived through analytic continuation in complex parameters.
model_or_system: The analysis is applied to various quantum systems, including Conformal Field Theory (CFT) boundary states, fermionic and bosonic Gaussian states, and general bipartite pure states in finite-dimensional Hilbert spaces.
key_observables: Entanglement Entropy ($S_E$), Pseudo Entropy ($S$), Pseudo-Rényi Entropies ($S_n$), and the reduced transition matrix ($	au_A$).
important_parameters: Complex parameters ($z = x + iy$) used for analytic continuation, and system parameters related to boundary conditions or time evolution.
main_assumptions: The method assumes the reduced density matrix function is holomorphic on a domain in the complex parameter space, and convergence of the required Taylor series is assumed for the derived formulas to hold.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates the two-qubit example, comparing the real part of pseudo entropy, average entanglement entropy, and the excess pseudo entropy across a path parameter.
paper_structure: The paper builds from the definition of pseudo entropy for nonorthogonal states, develops the mathematical machinery using complex analysis (Cauchy-Riemann, Kramers-Kronig), derives general formulas for real/imaginary parts and Rényi generalizations, and concludes with applications to CFT and Gaussian states.
why_interesting: The rigorous mathematical framework connecting standard entanglement measures to complex extensions via analytic continuation is highly relevant for understanding non-equilibrium dynamics and boundary effects in quantum field theories.
